category_title: Students with severe intellectual disability (SID) using pre-symbolic or limited symbolic communication and idiosyncratic repair strategies
scenario_title: Preempting and topic shifting during simple questions
minimal_context: The student is answering a simple question about the next classroom activity by pointing to graphic symbols.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It is time for our next activity. Look at the graphic symbols. Which one do you want?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Makes eye contact, produces a vocal sound, and points to one of the graphic symbols, waiting for the partner to lead the interaction.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: I see you pointing at the table.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Uses repetition as a repair strategy by pointing to the graphic symbol again and changing facial expressions to convey the message.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's just put the symbols away and go wash our hands now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Exhibits communication arrest, dropping eye contact, lowering hands, and completely shutting down any further attempts to communicate or respond.)

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: It is time for our next activity. Look at the graphic symbols. Which one do you want?

STUDENT: (Makes eye contact, produces a vocal sound, and points to one of the graphic symbols, waiting for the partner to lead the interaction.)

TUTOR: I see you pointing at the table.

STUDENT: (Uses repetition as a repair strategy by pointing to the graphic symbol again and changing facial expressions to convey the message.)

TUTOR: Let's just put the symbols away and go wash our hands now.

STUDENT: (Exhibits communication arrest, dropping eye contact, lowering hands, and completely shutting down any further attempts to communicate or respond.)

task.content: Answering simple questions using graphic symbols and conventional gestures

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When a partner responds but changes the subject away from the student's intent ('topic shift')
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Remains with a limited understanding that the message transfer was unsuccessful, with no clue to the nature of the failure

behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Depend mainly on their communication partners for leading interactions and refer mainly to responses rather than to initiations
